chapters.title: Microsoft 365 as a distributed decision engine
Automation, compliance theater and the certification trap
The litmus test and system-first model

takeaways: Microsoft 365 is one platform that behaves like a distributed decision engine, so governing it by tool ownership guarantees conflicting policies and drift.
Policies, labels and certifications are not governance on their own; governance needs intent, enforcement by default and feedback loops with named owners of the consequences.

Replace portal-based roles with system governors such as a platform governance lead, an identity and access steward and an information flow owner, backed by monthly health and quarterly blast radius reviews.
hook: Many organizations blame Microsoft 365 complexity when governance fails, but the real gap is unclear accountability and fragmented tool ownership. This episode helps IT leaders and governance owners replace tool-first thinking with a system-first operating model, clear outcome owners and a simple litmus test for every change.
